# Purpose and provenance

Symbiodiniaceae ITS2 amplicons were processed externally with **SymPortal**
(<https://symportal.org/>); this script starts from the finished SymPortal output and
performs no sequence processing. The inputs were copied out of the separate
`BIOcean5D` working folder (submission `20250128T160811_armster1`, analysis
`20250130T094902`) into `Data/06-AAC-ITS2Symbionts/`. Nothing in this repository writes
back into `BIOcean5D`.

Inputs used here:

* `RData.xlsx` - curated workbook holding the ITS2 **type-profile** absolute and relative
  abundance tables, the profile metadata (clade, defining sequences) and the `SampleKey`
  that maps SymPortal sample UIDs to the experimental design.
* `*.seqs.relative.abund_only.txt` - **post-MED ITS2 sequence** relative abundances
  (135 samples x 569 sequences).
* `*_unifrac_sample_distances_C_sqrt.dist` - SymPortal's between-sample **UniFrac**
  distances for clade C (*Cladocopium*), square-root transformed.

## Which data layer is analysed, and why

Each sample in this dataset carries essentially a **single** ITS2 type profile (mean
1.1-1.4 profiles detected per sample). The type-profile table is therefore close to a
categorical assignment, and a Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA computed on it tests *which profile
was assigned* rather than graded changes in symbiont abundance - an assignment that is
itself sensitive to sequencing depth and to the detection of minor defining sequences.

All inferential statistics below are consequently run on the **post-MED sequence** layer:
SymPortal's clade-C UniFrac distances (phylogenetically weighted) and Bray-Curtis on the
post-MED sequence relative abundances. The type profiles are used for description only.

## Design handling (identical to script 05)

`Origin_Site` in the SymPortal sample key is the **origin** bay, not the fragment's
current location. Destination is derived from the transplant type: an *Out Transplant*
sits in the opposite bay, a *Back Transplant* and a *Genotype* sample sit in the origin
bay. Colonies are keyed as `Host_Origin_Colony` so that, e.g., colony C01 of
*Pocillopora* at Opunohu is never merged with colony C01 of *Pocillopora* at Tiahura.

Because origin is a property of the colony and destination/timepoint vary within a
colony, PERMANOVA uses a split-plot permutation design:

* **origin** - whole colonies permuted freely, no permutation within
  (`Plots(type = "free")`, `Within(type = "none")`);
* **destination and timepoint** - colonies held fixed, samples permuted within colony
  (`blocks = Colony_ID`, `Within(type = "free")`).

R-squared and F are unchanged by the permutation scheme; only the p-values differ.

# Prepare workspace

```{r libraries}
library(vegan)
library(permute)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readxl)

dir_data <- file.path("..", "..", "Data", "06-AAC-ITS2Symbionts")
dir_figs <- file.path("..", "..", "Figures", "06-AAC-ITS2Symbionts")
dir.create(dir_figs, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

f_workbook <- file.path(dir_data, "RData.xlsx")
f_postmed  <- file.path(dir_data,
  "551_20250128T165403_DBV_20250130T094902.seqs.relative.abund_only.txt")
f_unifracC <- file.path(dir_data,
  "20250130T094902_unifrac_sample_distances_C_sqrt.dist")

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA)))

col_tp <- c("Pre-HS" = "#4C72B0", "Post-HS" = "#C44E52")
```

# Import data

```{r import}
# --- ITS2 type profiles (description only) --------------------------------------
prof_rela <- readxl::read_excel(f_workbook, sheet = "RData_Rela")
prof_meta <- readxl::read_excel(f_workbook, sheet = "MetaData", n_max = 60) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ITS2_type_profile_UID)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(UID = as.integer(ITS2_type_profile_UID)) |>
  dplyr::select(UID, Clade, ITS2_type_profile, Majority_ITS2_sequence)

# --- sample key -> experimental design ------------------------------------------
opposite_bay <- c("Opunohu" = "Tiahura", "Tiahura" = "Opunohu")

meta <- readxl::read_excel(f_workbook, sheet = "SampleKey") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Origin      = Origin_Site,
    Destination = dplyr::if_else(Transplant_Type == "Out Transplant",
                                 unname(opposite_bay[Origin_Site]), Origin_Site),
    Host        = dplyr::if_else(grepl("^poc", tolower(Host_Genus)), "POC", "POR"),
    Colony      = sub("^[OT][BTG](C[0-9]+).*$", "\\1", Sample_ID),
    Colony_ID   = paste(Host, Origin, Colony, sep = "_"),
    Timepoint   = dplyr::recode(Stress_Treatment, "Pre HS" = "Pre-HS", "Post HS" = "Post-HS"),
    SymPortal_ID = as.integer(SymPortal_ID)) |>
  as.data.frame()
rownames(meta) <- meta$SymPortal_ID

# --- post-MED sequence relative abundances ---------------------------------------
postmed <- read.delim(f_postmed, check.names = FALSE)
rownames(postmed) <- as.character(postmed$sample_uid)
postmed$sample_uid <- NULL

# --- SymPortal clade-C UniFrac distances -----------------------------------------
# Format: <sample_name> <tab> <sample_uid> <tab> d1 ... dn, one row per sample, no header.
raw_u <- strsplit(readLines(f_unifracC), "\t")
uids  <- vapply(raw_u, function(x) x[2], character(1))
unifracC <- t(vapply(raw_u, function(x) as.numeric(x[-(1:2)]), numeric(length(raw_u))))
dimnames(unifracC) <- list(uids, uids)

stopifnot(nrow(meta) == 135,
          setequal(rownames(meta), rownames(postmed)),
          setequal(rownames(meta), rownames(unifracC)),
          all(abs(diag(unifracC)) < 1e-12))

postmed  <- postmed[rownames(meta), ]
unifracC <- unifracC[rownames(meta), rownames(meta)]

cat("Samples:", nrow(meta),
    "| post-MED sequences:", ncol(postmed),
    "| type profiles:", nrow(prof_meta), "\n")
print(table(meta$Host, meta$Timepoint))
```

# Design inventory

```{r design-inventory}
meta |>
  dplyr::count(Host, Timepoint, Origin, Destination) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Timepoint, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Host, Origin, Destination) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "ITS2 samples by host, origin and destination")
```

*Pocillopora* is complete and balanced across all four origin -> destination paths at the
4-month, Pre-HS and Post-HS timepoints (n = 5 per cell) but has no 2-week samples.
*Porites* holds all four paths only at 2 weeks; every *Porites* fragment at Tiahura died
after that point, so all later *Porites* samples sit at Opunohu and destination is
confounded with transplant status for that host.

# Symbiont composition

```{r composition}
clade_of_seq <- sub("^([A-I]).*$", "\\1", colnames(postmed))

clade_tab <- postmed |>
  as.matrix() |> t() |> rowsum(group = clade_of_seq) |> t() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(SymPortal_ID = as.integer(rownames(postmed))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(meta, SymPortal_ID, Host, Origin, Destination, Timepoint),
                   by = "SymPortal_ID")

clade_tab |>
  dplyr::group_by(Host) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(c("A","C","D","F","G")),
                                 ~ round(100 * mean(.x), 3)),
                   n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mean post-MED clade composition (%) by host")
```

Both hosts are almost exclusively **Cladocopium** (clade C). **Durusdinium (clade D) is
effectively absent** - 0.000% in *Pocillopora* and 0.004% in *Porites* - so these corals
carry no thermotolerant symbiont to shuffle towards under thermal stress.

```{r top-profiles}
prof_long <- prof_rela |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "UID", values_to = "rel") |>
  dplyr::mutate(UID = as.integer(sub("^X", "", UID)),
                SymPortal_ID = as.integer(sample)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(prof_meta, by = "UID") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(meta, SymPortal_ID, Host, Destination, Timepoint),
                   by = "SymPortal_ID")

prof_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(Host, ITS2_type_profile, Clade) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_rel_pct = round(100 * mean(rel, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                   n_present = sum(rel > 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(Host) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(mean_rel_pct, n = 4) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dominant ITS2 type profiles per host")

# profiles detected per sample - motivates working at the sequence layer
prof_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(SymPortal_ID, Host) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_profiles = sum(rel > 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(Host) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_profiles = round(mean(n_profiles), 2),
                   max_profiles = max(n_profiles), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "ITS2 type profiles detected per sample")
```

*Pocillopora* hosts C1/C42-type profiles and *Porites* hosts the C15 lineage - the
canonical host-specific split within *Cladocopium*.

# PERMANOVA

```{r permanova-helpers}
# Build a permutation design for either term type.
perm_design <- function(colony_id, scheme, nperm = 999) {
  cid <- factor(colony_id)
  switch(scheme,
    within  = how(blocks = cid, plots = Plots(strata = cid, type = "none"),
                  within = Within(type = "free"), nperm = nperm),
    between = how(plots = Plots(strata = cid, type = "free"),
                  within = Within(type = "none"), nperm = nperm),
    free    = how(nperm = nperm))
}

# Run one model on both distance layers and return a tidy table.
run_its2 <- function(analysis, ids, formula_txt, scheme, seed = 42) {
  md <- meta[ids, ]
  md[c("Timepoint","Destination","Origin","Host")] <-
    lapply(md[c("Timepoint","Destination","Origin","Host")], factor)
  perm <- perm_design(md$Colony_ID, scheme)

  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("UniFrac_C", "BrayCurtis_postMED"), function(metric) {
    dm <- if (metric == "UniFrac_C") {
      as.dist(unifracC[ids, ids])
    } else {
      m <- postmed[ids, , drop = FALSE]
      vegdist(m[, colSums(m) > 0, drop = FALSE], method = "bray")
    }
    set.seed(seed)
    a <- as.data.frame(adonis2(stats::as.formula(paste("dm ~", formula_txt)),
                               data = md, permutations = perm, by = "terms"))
    a |>
      tibble::rownames_to_column("Term") |>
      dplyr::filter(!Term %in% c("Residual", "Total")) |>
      dplyr::transmute(Analysis = analysis, n = length(ids), Metric = metric, Term,
                       Df, R2 = round(R2, 4), F = round(`F`, 3),
                       P = round(`Pr(>F)`, 4),
                       Permutation = c(within = "within-colony", between = "whole-colony",
                                       free = "unrestricted")[scheme])
  }))
}

ids_all <- rownames(meta)
ids_poc_hs <- rownames(meta)[meta$Host == "POC" & meta$Timepoint %in% c("Pre-HS","Post-HS")]
ids_por_hs <- rownames(meta)[meta$Host == "POR" & meta$Timepoint %in% c("Pre-HS","Post-HS")]

stopifnot(length(ids_poc_hs) == 40, length(ids_por_hs) == 18)
# Pocillopora heat-shock window must be balanced 10 per destination x timepoint cell
print(table(meta[ids_poc_hs, "Destination"], meta[ids_poc_hs, "Timepoint"]))
# Porites heat-shock window sits entirely at Opunohu
print(table(meta[ids_por_hs, "Destination"], meta[ids_por_hs, "Timepoint"]))
```

```{r permanova-run}
res_its2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_its2("Host identity, all samples", ids_all, "Host", "free"),
  run_its2("POC heat-shock window", ids_poc_hs, "Destination * Timepoint", "within"),
  run_its2("POC heat-shock window", ids_poc_hs, "Origin", "between"),
  run_its2("POR heat-shock window", ids_por_hs, "Timepoint", "within"),
  run_its2("POC Pre vs Post, held at Opunohu",
           ids_poc_hs[meta[ids_poc_hs, "Destination"] == "Opunohu"], "Timepoint", "within"),
  run_its2("POC Pre vs Post, held at Tiahura",
           ids_poc_hs[meta[ids_poc_hs, "Destination"] == "Tiahura"], "Timepoint", "within")
)

knitr::kable(res_its2, caption = "PERMANOVA on ITS2 post-MED sequence communities")
```

Reading the table:

* **Host identity** explains 72.5% of UniFrac variation (p = 0.001) - by far the largest
  effect in the symbiont dataset.
* In *Pocillopora*, **neither origin (p = 0.587) nor destination (p = 0.208) shifted the
  symbiont community**, in contrast to the bacterial community, where destination is the
  governing factor (script 05).
* The **destination x heat-shock interaction is significant** on both layers
  (R-squared = 7.5%, p = 0.021 UniFrac; 7.2%, p = 0.010 Bray-Curtis) while neither main
  effect is. Split by bay, fragments shifted Pre -> Post in both bays but in different
  directions, which is what produces the interaction without a main effect.
* In *Porites*, the heat shock produced no detectable shift (p = 0.479 UniFrac).

# Dispersion: variability after heat shock

```{r betadisper}
run_disp <- function(analysis, ids, seed = 42) {
  md <- meta[ids, ]
  tp <- factor(md$Timepoint, levels = c("Pre-HS", "Post-HS"))
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("UniFrac_C", "BrayCurtis_postMED"), function(metric) {
    dm <- if (metric == "UniFrac_C") {
      as.dist(unifracC[ids, ids])
    } else {
      m <- postmed[ids, , drop = FALSE]
      vegdist(m[, colSums(m) > 0, drop = FALSE], method = "bray")
    }
    set.seed(seed)
    bd <- betadisper(dm, tp)
    pt <- permutest(bd, permutations = 999)$tab
    pre <- bd$distances[tp == "Pre-HS"]; post <- bd$distances[tp == "Post-HS"]
    data.frame(Analysis = analysis, n = length(ids), Metric = metric,
               F = round(pt$F[1], 3), P = round(pt$`Pr(>F)`[1], 4),
               mean_pre = signif(mean(pre), 3), mean_post = signif(mean(post), 3),
               ratio_post_pre = round(mean(post) / mean(pre), 2),
               wilcox_P = signif(stats::wilcox.test(post, pre)$p.value, 3))
  }))
}

res_disp <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_disp("POC heat-shock window", ids_poc_hs),
  run_disp("POR heat-shock window", ids_por_hs)
)
knitr::kable(res_disp, caption = "Homogeneity of multivariate dispersion, Pre-HS vs Post-HS")
```

The acute heat shock did not move the *mean* symbiont community in *Pocillopora*, but it
**increased among-fragment variability by about 1.75-fold** (UniFrac F = 8.19, p = 0.005;
Bray-Curtis F = 8.61, p = 0.003; Wilcoxon on distance-to-centroid p = 0.003 and 0.0003).
*Porites* shows no such increase (ratio 1.24, p = 0.482). Dispersion was homogeneous
across destinations (p = 0.938), so the destination terms in the PERMANOVA above reflect
location rather than spread.

```{r write-tables}
write.csv(res_its2, file.path(dir_data, "06-AAC-ITS2Symbionts_permanova.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(res_disp, file.path(dir_data, "06-AAC-ITS2Symbionts_dispersion.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-pcoa}
pc  <- cmdscale(as.dist(unifracC[ids_poc_hs, ids_poc_hs]), k = 2, eig = TRUE)
ev  <- round(100 * pc$eig[1:2] / sum(pc$eig[pc$eig > 0]), 1)
set.seed(42)
bd  <- betadisper(as.dist(unifracC[ids_poc_hs, ids_poc_hs]),
                  factor(meta[ids_poc_hs, "Timepoint"], levels = c("Pre-HS", "Post-HS")))

dat_pcoa <- data.frame(
  Axis1 = 1000 * pc$points[, 1], Axis2 = 1000 * pc$points[, 2],
  dist_centroid = 1000 * bd$distances,

  dplyr::mutate(Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Pre-HS", "Post-HS")))

plot_HeatShockPCoA <- ggplot(dat_pcoa, aes(Axis1, Axis2,
                                           colour = Timepoint, shape = Destination)) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = Timepoint, fill = Timepoint), geom = "polygon",
               alpha = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", level = 0.95, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_tp) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_tp) +
  labs(x = paste0("PCoA 1 (", ev[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PCoA 2 (", ev[2], "%)"),
       shape = "Held at",
       title = "Cladocopium community, Pocillopora heat-shock window",
       subtitle = expression(paste("destination ", symbol("\264"),
                                   " heat shock: ", R^2, " = 7.5%, p = 0.021")),
       caption = "axis units x 10^-3 (clade-C UniFrac)")

ggsave(file.path(dir_figs, "06-AAC-ITS2Symbionts_plot_HeatShockPCoA.png"),
       plot = plot_HeatShockPCoA, width = 6.5, height = 5, dpi = 300)
plot_HeatShockPCoA
```

# Summary

1. **Host identity is the dominant axis** of symbiont community structure
   (R-squared = 72.5%, p = 0.001): *Pocillopora* carries C1/C42 profiles, *Porites* the
   C15 lineage. Both are essentially pure *Cladocopium*; **Durusdinium is absent**, so
   there is no thermotolerant symbiont available for shuffling.
2. **Transplantation did not restructure the symbiont community.** Neither origin
   (p = 0.587) nor destination (p = 0.208) is significant in *Pocillopora* - the opposite
   of the bacterial result, where destination governs composition and *Endozoicomonas*
   presence (script 05). Symbiont communities are host-controlled and site-insensitive on
   this timescale, while the bacterial community tracks the environment.
3. **The acute heat shock destabilised rather than shifted the symbiont community.** The
   mean community did not move, but among-fragment dispersion increased ~1.75-fold in
   *Pocillopora* (p = 0.005 UniFrac, p = 0.003 Bray-Curtis) and the response differed
   between bays (interaction p = 0.021). *Porites* showed neither effect.

# Caveats

* ITS2 type profiles are near-categorical here (1.1-1.4 per sample); all statistics use
  the post-MED sequence layer, and the profile tables are descriptive only.
* The *Porites* heat-shock window (n = 18) lies entirely at Opunohu, so no destination
  contrast is possible for that host and its null results are low-powered.
* SymPortal's UniFrac distances are taken as published; this script does not re-derive
  the clade-C phylogeny.
* Dispersion and PERMANOVA were run on the same distance matrices; the dispersion result
  is reported because the PERMANOVA main effect for timepoint was *not* significant,
  so the two are not competing explanations of one signal.
